authors: A. Markowitz, R. Abuaamoud, S. Ben Ayed, A. Rupe, R. Yang, T. Kliphuis, V.V. Vesselinov
title: AI-augmented geothermal model for scalable energy uncertainties in buildings
abstract: This work presents a scalable software tool for predicting geothermal energy use in residential buildings under conditions that demand fast, physically informed simulations. Using a reduced-order model benchmarked against EnergyPlus and datasets generated with Latin Hypercube Sampling, Saltelli, and eFast methods, the study applies XGBoost to predict energy usage with high accuracy while preserving computational efficiency.

authors: P. Lara, N.R. Ranasinghe, V.V. Vesselinov, C.W. Johnson
title: Deep-Embedded-Clustering of Microseismicity Identifies Multiple Failure Mechanisms at The Geysers Geothermal Field
abstract: Enhanced Geothermal Systems regularly produce microseismic activity as fluid injection perturbs the thermo-hydromechanical state of the reservoir. This study applies Deep Embedded Clustering to waveform, spectrogram, and cepstrogram data from the 2011–2012 stimulation of the Prati-32 EGS well at The Geysers, identifying three distinct failure classes and helping relate waveform characteristics to underlying physical mechanisms.

authors: E.E. Jafarov, H. Genet, V.V. Vesselinov, V. Briones, A. Kabeer, A.L. Mullen, B. Maglio, T. Carman, R. Rutter, J. Clein, C.-C. Chang, D. Teber, T. Smith, J.M. Rady, C. Schädel, J.D. Watts, B.M. Rogers, S.M. Natali
title: Estimation of above- and below-ground ecosystem parameters for DVM-DOS-TEM v0.7.0 using MADS v1.7.3
abstract: This study develops an automated parameter calibration method for the DVM-DOS-TEM ecosystem model designed for high-latitude permafrost regions. Using the MADS software package, the authors calibrate rate-limiting parameters controlling carbon and nitrogen dynamics in boreal forests, demonstrating that hierarchical sequential calibration can effectively recover known parameter values even when initial guesses are perturbed by substantial margins.

authors: T.L. Kliphuis, A. Markowitz, R. Yang, V.V. Vesselinov
title: GeoDAWN To GeoTGo: From Complex Data To Decisions Related To Geothermal Prospectivity
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Kliphuis 2025 GeoDAWN To GeoTGo From Complex Data To Decisions Related To Geothermal
abstract: This work presents a geothermal prospectivity workflow that moves from complex heterogeneous datasets to more defensible exploration decisions through physics-informed AI/ML. Building on the GeoTGo platform, it integrates geological, geophysical, geochemical, and structural information to reduce subjectivity, improve transparency, and support scalable community-oriented geothermal resource assessment.

authors: V.V. Vesselinov, H. Jasperson, T.L. Kliphuis
title: Machine-Learning Methods and Tools Designed for Community-Based Equitable and Inclusive Geothermal Development
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Vesselinov 2024 Machine-Learning Methods and Tools Designed for Community-Based Equitable and Inclusive.pdf
abstract: This work presents machine-learning methods and software tools aimed at supporting community-based, equitable, and inclusive geothermal development. Built around the GeoTGo platform, it integrates diverse geological, geochemical, and geophysical data with interactive analysis workflows to help communities identify, evaluate, and communicate geothermal opportunities in a more transparent and accessible way.

authors: V.V. Vesselinov, T.L. Kliphuis
title: ChemML: Physics-Informed AI/ML of Geochemical Datasets for Characterization, Parameterization, and Prediction of Contaminant Transport and Remediation Processes
url: https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=K5pN4JAAAAAJ&citation_for_view=K5pN4JAAAAAJ:9yKSN-GCB0IC
abstract: This work describes ChemML as a physics-informed AI/ML framework for analyzing geochemical datasets and improving the characterization, parameterization, and prediction of contaminant transport and remediation processes. The approach emphasizes robust, trustworthy, and defensible science-informed models that can overcome limitations of traditional geochemical simulations while supporting cloud-based environmental decision and remediation workflows.

authors: D. O'Malley, S.Y. Greer, A. Pachalieva, W. Hao, D. Harp, V.V. Vesselinov
title: DPFEHM: a differentiable subsurface physics simulator
url: https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.04560
abstract: DPFEHM is a Julia-based simulator for subsurface physics that incorporates automatic differentiation capabilities for efficient modeling of multiphase flow, transport, and wave equation phenomena in hydrogeological systems.

authors: K.C. Solander, C.J. Talsma, V.V. Vesselinov
title: The drivers and predictability of wildfire re-burns in the western United States (US)
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Solander et al 2023 The drivers and predictability of wildfire re-burns in the western United States.pdf
abstract: Evidence is mounting that the effectiveness of using prescribed burns as a management tactic may be diminishing due to the higher incidence of wildfire re-burns. The development of predictive models of re-burns is thus essential to better understand their primary drivers so that forest management practices can be updated to account for these events.

title: A Progress Report on GeoThermalCloud: Framework An Open-Source Machine Learning Based Tool for Discovery, Exploration, and Development of Hidden Geothermal Resources
authors: B. Ahmmed, M.K. Mudunuru, L.P. Frash, V.V. Vesselinov
url: https://pangea.stanford.edu/ERE/pdf/IGAstandard/SGW/2023/Ahmmed1.pdf
abstract: This progress report presents GeoThermalCloud as an open-source machine-learning framework for geothermal resource discovery, exploration, and development. The platform is designed to analyze large and diverse geothermal datasets, assimilate model simulations, identify hidden geothermal signatures, guide data acquisition, and support lower-risk exploration and production decisions through tools developed under its resource-exploration and enhanced-geothermal-system workflows.

authors: J. Bennett, J. Ogland-Hand, K. Cox, P. Johnson, E. Middleton, A. Pompilio, S. Samal, C. Talsma, V.V. Vesselinov, K. Ellett, R. Middleton
title: Beam Me Up SCO2TPRO: A Comparison to the FE/NETL CO2 Saline Storage Cost Model and Updates on Tool Development
url: https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4275200
abstract: In order to meet climate goals, carbon capture and storage (CCS) needs to be developed at a large scale. A major factor in developing CCS is where CO2 can be safely stored, and for what cost. To assist with this determination, we have developed the professional version of the Sequestration of CO2 Tool (SCO2TPRO). In this paper, we introduce SCO2TPRO and compare its performance to the FE/NETL CO2 Saline Storage Cost Model. Finally, we present on-going development progress including developing new training data with the STOMP reservoir simulator, advanced reduced order models, and refined geologic inputs.

authors: C.J. Talsma, K.E. Bennett, V.V. Vesselinov
title: Characterizing Drought Behavior in the Colorado River Basin Using Unsupervised Machine Learning
abstract: Drought is a major concern in the Colorado River Basin because of the region’s high social and economic dependence on water resources and the uncertainty of future drought under climate change. This study combines Earth System Model climate simulations, the Variable Infiltration Capacity hydrologic model, and an unsupervised NMFk workflow to identify sub-watersheds with important changes in snowpack, snowmelt timing, precipitation, and evapotranspiration.

authors: V.V. Vesselinov, B. Ahmmed, M. Mudunuru, S. Karra, R. Middleton
title: Discovering hidden geothermal signatures using non-negative matrix factorization with customized k-means clustering
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Vesselinov et al 2022 Discovering Hidden Geothermal Signatures using Non-negative Matrix Factorization with Customized k-means Clustering.pdf
abstract: Discovery of hidden geothermal resources is challenging. It requires the mining of large datasets with diverse data attributes representing subsurface hydrogeological and geothermal conditions. The commonly used play fairway analysis approach typically incorporates subject-matter expertise to analyze regional data to estimate geothermal characteristics and favorability.

authors: V.V. Vesselinov, B. Ahmmed, M. Mudunuru, S. Karra, R. Middleton
title: GeoThermalCloud: Machine Learning for Discovery, Exploration, and Development of Hidden Geothermal Resources
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Vesselinov 2022 GeoThermalCloud Machine Learning for Discovery, Exploration, and Development of Hidden Geothermal Resources.pdf
abstract: This workshop paper presents GeoThermalCloud as an open-source, cloud-based machine-learning framework for geothermal resource discovery, exploration, and development. The platform is designed to fuse diverse geothermal datasets with multi-physics models, discover hidden geothermal signatures, prioritize high-value data acquisition, and reduce the cost and risk of geothermal resource assessment.

authors: M. Mudunuru, V.V. Vesselinov, B. Ahmmed
title: GeoThermalCloud: Machine learning for geothermal resource exploration
source: Journal of Machine Learning for Modeling and Computing
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Mudunuru et al 2022 Geothermalcloud - Machine learning for geothermal resource exploration.pdf
abstract: This work presents GeoThermalCloud as a machine-learning framework for geothermal resource exploration, with an emphasis on discovering blind hydrothermal systems that lack clear surface expression. The study highlights how data-driven methods can reduce the time, cost, and uncertainty associated with conventional exploration by integrating and analyzing diverse geothermal datasets.

authors: H. Wu, D. O'Malley, J.K. Golden, V.V. Vesselinov
title: Inverse Analysis with Variational Autoencoders: A Comparison of Shallow and Deep Networks
source: Journal of Machine Learning for Modeling and Computing

abstract: Characterization of reservoir properties, e.g., hydraulic conductivity, is of essential importance in hydrogeology, such as groundwater resources managementand subsurface contaminant Wu et al. remediation. Moreover, spatial heterogeneities of reservoir properties are present from pore to reservoir scale, and understanding the heterogeneity effects on fluid flow is critical (Doughty and Pruess, 2004; Jayne et al., 2019).

authors: M. Ahmmed, V.V. Vesselinov
title: Machine learning and a process model to better characterize hidden geothermal resources
url: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361052032_Machine_learning_and_a_process_model_to_better_characterize_hidden_geothermal_resources
abstract: The Tularosa Basin in New Mexico has significant geothermal potential. This paper curated data from the Department of Energy's Geothermal Data Repository and analyzed them with a machine learning based framework, GeoThermalCloud (GTC), to find prospective geothermal locations. GTC discovers prospective geothermal locations and finds key parameters defining these prospectivities. Also, we found that these prospectivities are consistent with an existing comprehensive play fairway analysis. Finally, we discussed a coupling strategy between a process model (Burns equation) and GTC to obtain a better understanding about the geothermal conditions in the study area.

authors: B. Ahmmed, V.V. Vesselinov
title: Machine learning and shallow groundwater chemistry to identify geothermal prospects in the Great Basin
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Ahmmed & Vesselinov 2022 Machine learning and shallow groundwater chemistry to identify geothermal prospects in the Great Basin.pdf
abstract: This study identifies geothermal prospects in the Great Basin using shallow groundwater geochemistry as a proxy for geothermal prospectivity. By processing sparse geochemical measurements from more than 14,000 locations, the work shows how machine learning can uncover hidden information in regional chemistry datasets and help prioritize promising areas for geothermal exploration.

authors: V.V. Vesselinov, M. Mudunuru, B. Ahmmed, S. Karra, D. O'Malley
title: Machine Learning to Discover, Characterize, and Produce Geothermal Energy
source: Machine Learning Applications in Subsurface Energy Resource Management
abstract: This work describes how machine learning can support the discovery, characterization, and production of geothermal energy, an abundant renewable resource with major potential for grid resilience and domestic energy security. It emphasizes the role of data-driven methods in reducing exploration and development risk, improving resource understanding, and supporting more affordable geothermal deployment.

authors: B. Ahmmed, V.V. Vesselinov, M.K. Mudunuru
title: SmartTensors: Unsupervised and physics-informed machine learning framework for the geoscience applications
source: Second International Meeting for Applied Geoscience & Energy
url: https://doi.org/10.1190/image2022-w8-01.1
abstract: SmartTensors is presented as an unsupervised and physics-informed machine learning framework for geoscience applications built around constrained matrix and tensor factorization methods. The platform emphasizes robustness and interpretability and is demonstrated on geothermal prospectivity analysis in the Great Basin, where regional geochemical data are used to infer subsurface reservoir characteristics.

authors: B. Ahmmed, M.K. Mudunuru, S. Karra, S.C. James, V.V. Vesselinov
title: A comparative study of machine learning models for predicting the state of reactive mixing
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Ahmmed et al 2021 A comparative study of machine learning models for predicting the state of reactive mixing.pdf
abstract: Mixing phenomena are important mechanisms controlling flow, species transport, and reaction processes in fluids and porous media. Accurate predictions of reactive mixing are critical for many Earth and environmental science problems such as contaminant fate and remediation, macroalgae growth, and plankton biomass growth. To investigate the evolution of mixing dynamics under different scenarios (e.g.,anisotropy, fluctuating velocity fields), a finite-element-based numerical model was built to solve the fast, irreversible bimolecular reaction-diffusion equations to simulate a range of reactive-mixing scenarios.

authors: G. Morra, E. Bozdag, M. Knepley, L. Rass, V.V. Vesselinov
title: A Tectonic Shift in Analytics and Computing Is Coming
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Morra et al 2021 A Tectonic Shift in Analytics and Computing Is Coming.pdf
abstract: This article argues that artificial intelligence combined with high-performance computing is poised to change how geoscientists extract knowledge from large and complex datasets. It highlights a broader transition toward data-driven scientific workflows capable of accelerating discovery, interpretation, and decision support across Earth and environmental sciences.

authors: S.W. Fleming, V.V. Vesselinov, A.G. Goodbody
title: Augmenting geophysical interpretation of data-driven operational water supply forecast modeling for a western US river using a hybrid machine learning approach

abstract: In the largely dry and increasingly heavily populated western US, operational modeling systems for seasonal river runoff volume forecasting are key elements of the practical water and hydropower management infrastructure. Explainability of model results in terms of known hydroclimatic processes and conditions is a core requirement for these systems.

authors: V.V. Vesselinov, B. Ahmmed, M. Mudunuru, S. Karra, R. Middleton
title: Discovering the Hidden Geothermal Signatures of Southwest New Mexico
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Vesselinov et al 2021 Discovering the Hidden Geothermal Signatures of Southwest New Mexico.pdf
abstract: This work applies unsupervised machine learning to diverse regional datasets to identify hidden geothermal signatures in southwest New Mexico. By mining geological, geochemical, and geophysical information without relying solely on predefined labels, the study aims to reveal patterns associated with concealed geothermal systems and improve regional exploration targeting.

authors: D. O'Malley, J.K. Golden, V.V. Vesselinov
title: Learning to regularize with a variational autoencoder for hydrologic inverse analysis
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/O G V 2019 Learning to regularize with a variational autoencoder for hydrologic inverse analysis.pdf
abstract: Inverse problems often involve matching observational data using a physical model that takes a large number of parameters as input. These problems tend to be under-constrained and require regularization to impose additional structure on the solution in parameter space. A central difficulty in regularization is turning a complex conceptual model of this additional structure into a functional mathematical form to be used in the inverse analysis.

authors: S.W. Fleming, J.R. Watson, A. Ellenson, A.J. Cannon, V.V. Vesselinov
title: Machine learning in Earth and environmental science requires education and research policy reforms
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Fleming et al 2021 Machine learning in Earth and environmental science requires education and research policy reforms.pdf
abstract: This comment argues that advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning could significantly accelerate discovery and prediction in Earth and environmental science. It also contends that current research funding, training, and educational structures are not yet preparing enough geoscientists to use these tools effectively, and calls for policy and curriculum reforms to build that capacity.

authors: B. Ahmmed, M.K. Mudunuru, S. Karra, V.V. Vesselinov

abstract: Mineral trapping is pursued as a geological CO sequestration (GCS) mechanism because it permanently stores CO in solid phases or minerals.

authors: D.L. Siler, J.D. Pepin, V.V. Vesselinov, et al.
title: Machine learning to identify geologic factors associated with production in geothermal fields: A case-study using 3D geologic data, Brady geothermal field, Nevada
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Siler et al 2021 Machine learning to identify geologic factors associated with production in geothermal felds- a case‑study using 3D geologic data, Brady geothermal feld, Nevada.pdf
abstract: In this paper, we present an analysis using unsupervised machine learning (ML) to identify the key geologic factors that contribute to the geothermal production in Brady geothermal field. Brady is a hydrothermal system in northwestern Nevada that supports both electricity production and direct use of hydrothermal fluids. Transmissive fluid-flow pathways are relatively rare in the subsurface, but are critical components of hydrothermal systems like Brady and many other types of fluid-flow systems in fractured rock.

authors: M. Mehana, E. Guiltinan, V.V. Vesselinov, R. Middleton, J. Hyman, Q. Kang, H. Viswanathan
title: Machine-Learning Predictions of the Shale Wells’ Performance
source: Journal of Natural Gas Science and Engineering
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Mehana et al 2021 Machine-Learning Predictions of the Shale Wells Performance.pdf
abstract: The ultra-low permeability nature of shale reservoirs leads to an extended linear flow and necessitates horizontal wells with multi-stage engineered fractures to efficiently extract hydrocarbons resources. These artificiallygenerated and naturally-occurring fractures form complex networks that create complex flow regimes which control oil production. These fractures are neither identical nor equally-spaced, which leads to a production profile with a masked onset of the boundary-dominated flow.

authors: V.V. Vesselinov, M.K. Mudunuru, B. Ahmmed, S. Karra, R.S. Middleton
title: Discovering Signatures of Hidden Geothermal Resources based on Unsupervised Learning
url: https://montyv.github.io/papers/Vesselinov 2020 Discovering Signatures of Hidden Geothermal Resources based on Unsupervised Learning.pdf
abstract: This work explores unsupervised machine-learning methods for discovering hidden geothermal resource signatures from large, heterogeneous datasets. It emphasizes unbiased feature extraction without heavy dependence on prior labeling and demonstrates how these methods can help characterize geothermal systems and guide exploration decisions in geothermal study areas such as New Mexico and The Geysers.

authors: M.K. Mudunuru, H.S. Viswanathan, J. W. Carey, L. Chen, Q. Kang, S. Karra, V.V. Vesselinov, R.S. Middleton, P.A. Johnson

abstract: This work examines how geologic structure, state of stress, and well design affect hydrothermal fluid flow and energy production in geothermal systems. Using the NMFk unsupervised learning workflow within the SmartTensors framework, it identifies the reservoir and engineering parameters that most strongly control production and extracts characteristic energy-production signatures linked to subsurface conditions.
